nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NiFe LDH on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: First, the Ni foam (NF) substrate was cleaned multiple times with acetone, alcohol, and deionized water, respectively. Second, 0.75 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.18 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 2.5 mmol UREA, and 2.5 mmol NH4F were dissolved in 20 mL DI water with magnetic stirring. Subsequently, one piece of cleaned NF (1×3 cm²) was impregnated in the well-mixed solution. The pretreated above solution and NF were transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and heated to 120°C for 12 h. After it cooled to room temperature. Subsequently, the samples were picked out and washed several times with deionized water and alcohol, respectively, and then dried for direct use as electrodes.

nodes.name: Solvothermal anchoring of Ir single atoms
nodes.procedure: The single-atom Ir_sac-NiFe LDH catalyst was synthesized through a facile solvothermal reaction. First, 2 mg of IrCl3 was fully dissolved in the centrifuge tube with 20 mL of NaOH solution (0.01 M) and a piece of NiFe LDH@NF (30 mg of catalyst content). Then, the samples were subsequently transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 120°C for 2 h. After heating, the samples were rinsed with alcohol and DI water, respectively, and then dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: Typical hexagonal hydrotalcite structures indexed for Ir_sac-NiFe LDH with strong peaks at 11° and 23° ascribed to (003) and (006) planes; no new phase formed due to Ir doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S2 shows the XRD patterns of the NiFe LDH and Ir_sac-NiFe LDH samples. The typical hexagonal hydrotalcite structures are indexed for both samples, and no new phase is formed due to the Ir doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show nanosheet structure with smooth surface and sharp edges preserved after Ir doping, no obvious Ir deposition observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure S3) show the nanosheet structure with a smooth surface and sharp edges of the NiFe LDH sample. After Ir doping, the nanosheet structure remains...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanosheet structure preservation; HRTEM shows interplanar spacings of 0.268 nm and 0.251 nm indexed to (101) and (012) planes of NiFe LDH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the high-resolution TEM image (Figure 1d), the interplanar spacings of 0.268 and 0.251 nm can be indexed to the (101) and (012) planes of the NiFe LDH phase, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 binding energies at 60.7 and 63.6 eV; Ni 2p and Fe 2p peak shapes unchanged after Ir anchoring; O 1s deconvoluted into M-O, OH/O2, and adsorbed H2O peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S5d, the binding energies of 60.7 and 63.6 eV can be attributed to Ir 4f7/2 and Ir 4f5/2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Blue shifts of carboxylate stretching vibration and Ni-O vibration peaks in Ir_sac-NiFe LDH indicate increased Ni-O binding energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) is used to examine the changes in chemical bonds... The blue shifts of the carboxylate stretching vibration and Ni-O vibration peaks...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge shows valence Ir_sac-NiFe LDH < +3; Ni K-edge absorption higher after Ir doping (increased Ni valence); Fe K-edge shows higher valence in Ir_sac-NiFe LDH vs NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir L3-edge XANES spectra demonstrate that the valence state of as-prepared catalysts would decrease in the order IrO2 > IrCl3 > Ir_sac-NiFe LDH > Ir foil... It demonstrates that the absorption position of Ir_sac-NiFe LDH is higher than that of other samples...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge FT-EXAFS: Ir-O at 1.5-1.6 Å, contracted vs IrO2, no Ir-Ir bonding confirms atomic dispersion; Ni K-edge: decreased Ni-O peak strength indicates oxygen vacancies; Fe K-edge: Fe-O at 1.5 Å, Fe-M at 2.5 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b shows the Fourier-transformed Ir L3-edge EXAFS spectra. The main peak in the 1.5-1.6 Å range is attributed to the first shell of Ir-O coordination... No direct Ir-Ir bonding can be observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows NiII-OH at 447 cm⁻¹ and NiII-O at 517 cm⁻¹; phase transition at 1.45 V vs RHE for Ir_sac-NiFe LDH; high Iδ(NiIII-O)/Iν(NiIII-O) ratio of 1.46 indicates γ-NiOOH formation; O₂²⁻ band at 900-1200 cm⁻¹ confirms LOM; TMA⁺ trapping peaks at 753 and 951 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Under 1.4 V vs RHE, both NiFe LDH and Ir_sc-NiFe LDH in 1 M KOH show two characteristic peaks at ≈447 and 517 cm⁻¹, which are attributed to the A_lg stretching modes of NiII-OH and NiII-O...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir_sac-NiFe LDH shows O-O stretching at 1137 cm⁻¹ from 1.4 V indicating LOM; NiFe LDH shows *OOH at 1089 cm⁻¹ from 1.5 V indicating AEM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the potential increases to 1.4 V vs RHE, an absorption band at 1137 cm⁻¹ is observed, which is attributed to the O-O stretching vibration, indicating the generation of oxygen intermediates.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance used to estimate ECSA; Ir_sac-NiFe LDH shows 125 m²/g, 1.88× NiFe LDH (66.3 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA is estimated from the double-layer capacitance (C_dl) measurement in Figure S11. By mass normalizing the ECSA current at 1.2 V_RHE Ir_sac-NiFe LDH shows the highest activity (125 m²g⁻¹)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Nyquist plots show smallest charge transfer resistance R_ct for Ir_sac-NiFe LDH indicating fastest OER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the Nyquist plots, the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of Ir_sac-NiFe LDH is the smallest among all of the samples under the same conditions...
